title: NPC: 11 gov't agencies yet to fully explain data breaches
summary: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) said that 11 government agencies have yet to submit a full breach report following hacking incidents.

blocks.text: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) said that 11 government agencies have yet to submit a full breach report following hacking incidents.
NPC spokesperson Jose Amelito Belarmino II said that a total of 13 government agencies were reportedly hacked.

“Inaantay namin iyong full breach report ng ilang ahensiya. In fact, doon sa 13 na government agencies na na-breach at nag-report sa amin noong between November 9 to November 13, dalawa pa lamang iyong nagsusumite ng full breach report. So iyong iba po, wala pa pong isinusumite,” Belarmino said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing on Tuesday,

(We are waiting for the full breach report from several agencies. In fact, from the 13 government agencies that were breached from November 9 to 13, only two submitted their full breach report. The others have not submitted.)
The Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) were the two that reportedly already submitted, but Belarmino did not name the other 11.
In addition to the 13 agencies, the Department of Migrant Workers was also hacked. It must also submit a report.
Belarmino said that under the law, agencies that were hacked are required to submit a full report five days after they notify the NPC.
Failure to submit the full breach report was already a violation, said Belarmino. —LDF, GMA News
